children.summary: This section contains the report from PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, the independent registered public accounting firm, regarding their review of JPMorgan Chase & Co.'s interim financial statements as of June 30, 2023. The report confirms that the firm found no material modifications needed for the financial statements to conform with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles. It also references a previous audit conducted for the year ending December 31, 2022, which received an unqualified opinion. The report outlines the responsibilities of the firm's management and the scope of the review, emphasizing that it is less comprehensive than a full audit.

children.title: Consolidated Average Balance Sheets, Interest and Rates
children.summary: This section provides a detailed comparison of the consolidated average balance sheets, interest, and rates for JPMorgan Chase & Co. for the six months ending June 30, 2023, against the same period in 2022. It includes key financial metrics such as total interest-earning assets amounting to $3,280,619 million, net interest income of $42,714 million, and an interest rate spread of 2.00%. The section also covers average balances and interest earned across various asset categories, including deposits, loans, and securities, while offering insights into the bank's overall financial performance and interest rate trends during the specified periods.

children.title: Ytd table- ABS
children.summary: This section presents the consolidated average balance sheets, interest, and rates for JPMorgan Chase & Co. for the six months ending June 30, 2023, compared to the same period in 2022. It details average balances, interest earned, and annualized rates for various asset categories, including deposits, loans, and securities. Key figures include total interest-earning assets of $3,280,619 million with a net interest income of $42,714 million and an interest rate spread of 2.00%. The section also outlines liabilities, stockholders' equity, and provides insights into the bank's financial performance and interest rate trends over the specified periods.

children.title: Glossary of Terms and Acronyms and Line of Business Metrics
children.summary: This section provides a comprehensive glossary of terms and acronyms related to financial institution metrics, focusing on key performance indicators across various lines of business such as Consumer & Community Banking, Corporate & Investment Bank, Commercial Banking, and Asset & Wealth Management. It details specific metrics like debit and credit card sales volume, deposit margins, net mortgage servicing revenue, and assets under management. Additionally, it discusses revenue sources from lending, investment banking, and asset management, along with client and product classifications. The section also includes insights into mutual fund performance metrics and ratings, aiding in the evaluation of investment strategies.

children.title: Line of Business Metrics
children.summary: This section outlines key metrics for various lines of business within a financial institution, including Consumer & Community Banking (CCB), Corporate & Investment Bank (CIB), Commercial Banking (CB), and Asset & Wealth Management (AWM). Readers can learn about specific performance indicators such as debit and credit card sales volume, deposit margins, net mortgage servicing revenue, and assets under management. It details revenue sources across different banking segments, including lending, investment banking, and asset management, as well as the classification of clients and products. Additionally, it provides insights into mutual fund performance metrics and ratings, helping to assess the effectiveness of investment strategies.

children.title: Item 3. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk.
children.summary: This section refers readers to the Market Risk Management section of Management’s discussion and analysis and pages 131-138 of JPMorgan Chase’s 2022 Form 10-K for detailed quantitative and qualitative disclosures about market risk. It emphasizes the importance of understanding the firm's exposure to market fluctuations and the methodologies used to assess these risks. The section serves to inform stakeholders about the firm's risk management practices and the potential impact of market conditions on its financial performance.

children.title: Item 4. Controls and Procedures.
children.summary: This section discusses the evaluation of the effectiveness of JPMorgan Chase's disclosure controls and procedures, conducted by the Firm's management, including the CEO and CFO. They concluded that these controls were effective as of the report's end date. The section also highlights the Firm's commitment to maintaining high internal control standards, while acknowledging the inherent limitations that may lead to misstatements. Additionally, it notes the acquisition of assets and liabilities from First Republic Bank and confirms no significant changes in internal controls during the reporting period.

children.title: Part II – Other information
children.summary: Part II covers various important aspects of JPMorgan Chase's operations and compliance. It includes updates on legal proceedings, risk factors related to the acquisition of First Republic Bank, and confirms no unregistered sales of equity securities or defaults on senior securities. The section details the common share repurchase program, including the number of shares repurchased and compliance with trading arrangements. Additionally, it states that there are no mine safety disclosures required and lists key exhibits related to financial information and certifications under the Sarbanes-Oxley Act.

children.title: Item 1. Legal Proceedings.
children.summary: This section references the material legal proceedings involving JPMorgan Chase, directing readers to Note 26 of the Form 10-Q for updates on disclosures previously outlined in the 2022 Form 10-K. It highlights the importance of understanding ongoing legal matters that may impact the firm's operations and financial condition. The section serves to keep stakeholders informed about potential legal risks and their implications for the firm.

children.title: Item 1A. Risk Factors.
children.summary: This section discusses the risk factors affecting JPMorgan Chase, supplementing the previous disclosures in its 2022 Form 10-K. It highlights the potential risks associated with the acquisition of First Republic Bank, including uncertainties regarding integration costs, timeframes, and overall performance. The section emphasizes that the integration process may divert management resources and could lead to business disruptions, loss of clients, and challenges in maintaining employee relationships. Additionally, it notes that the descriptions provided are not exhaustive of all potential risks that could impact the Firm's financial condition and operations.

children.title: Item 2. Unregistered Sales of Equity Securities and Use of Proceeds.
children.summary: This section reports that JPMorgan Chase did not engage in any unregistered sales of equity securities during the three months ending June 30, 2023. It also references the common share repurchase program, which has a total authorization of up to $30 billion as approved by the Board of Directors. For further details on repurchases, readers are directed to the Capital Risk Management section of the current Form 10-Q and the previous year's Form 10-K.

children.title: Item 3. Defaults Upon Senior Securities.
children.summary: This section states that there were no defaults upon senior securities as of the report date. It also briefly mentions the common share repurchase program, detailing the number of shares repurchased, average prices, and the remaining authorized repurchase amount. Additionally, it notes compliance with Rule 10b5-1 regarding trading arrangements by directors and executive officers, and confirms no relevant trading arrangements were adopted or terminated in the second quarter of 2023. Lastly, it addresses compliance with the Iran Threat Reduction and Syria Human Rights Act, indicating no activities requiring disclosure were identified during the reporting period.

children.title: Item 4. Mine Safety Disclosures.
children.summary: Item 4, Mine Safety Disclosures, states that the section is not applicable, indicating that there are no mine safety-related disclosures required for the reporting period. This section typically addresses compliance with mine safety regulations and any incidents or violations, but in this case, it confirms the absence of such issues. Readers can learn that the firm has no mine safety disclosures to report for the specified period.

children.title: Item 5. Other Information.
children.summary: This section provides details on the common share repurchase program, including the total number of shares repurchased, average price per share, and the aggregate purchase price for the first and second quarters of 2023. It also outlines the remaining authorized repurchase amount under the $30 billion program. Additionally, it discusses Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangements adopted by directors and executive officers, including specific names, titles, adoption dates, and the number of shares to be sold. Furthermore, it includes a disclosure regarding compliance with the Iran Threat Reduction and Syria Human Rights Act, stating that no activities requiring disclosure occurred during the quarter ended June 30, 2023, except for a previously processed transaction that was an error.

children.title: Item 6. Exhibits.
children.summary: This section lists various exhibits related to financial information and certifications. Key exhibits include a letter regarding unaudited interim financial information, details on subsidiary guarantors, and multiple certifications under the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. It also includes XBRL (eXtensible Business Reporting Language) documents that provide structured financial data, such as consolidated statements of income and balance sheets for specific periods. The section clarifies which documents are filed and which are furnished, indicating their legal status under securities regulations.

children.title: Signature
children.summary: This section contains the official signature of JPMorgan Chase & Co. as required by the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. It includes the name and title of the signatory, Elena Korablina, who is the Managing Director and Firmwide Controller, serving as the Principal Accounting Officer. The date of the signature is August 3, 2023, indicating when the report was authorized. This section serves to validate the report and confirm its authenticity by an authorized representative of the registrant.

children.title: Exhibit 15
children.summary: Exhibit 15 contains a letter from PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP to the Securities and Exchange Commission dated August 3, 2023, regarding JPMorgan Chase & Co. It references multiple Registration Statements on Forms S-3 and S-8, detailing their respective numbers. The letter clarifies that the firm's report on interim financial information, included in the Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q, is incorporated by reference but should not be considered part of the Registration Statements as per Rule 436(c) of the Securities Act of 1933. This section is significant for understanding the compliance and regulatory framework surrounding JPMorgan's financial disclosures.

children.title: Exhibit 22
children.summary: Exhibit 22 details the guarantee provided by JPMorgan Chase & Co. for the debt securities issued by its subsidiary, JPMorgan Chase Financial Company LLC. It specifies that the subsidiary has issued Global Medium-Term Notes, Series A, which are fully guaranteed by JPMorgan Chase & Co. The section also mentions the potential for future debt securities and warrants to be issued under a specific Registration Statement on Form S-3, effective as of April 13, 2023. This information is crucial for understanding the financial obligations and guarantees associated with the subsidiary's securities.

children.title: Exhibit 31.1
children.summary: Exhibit 31.1 contains a certification by James Dimon, the CEO of JPMorgan Chase & Co., regarding the accuracy and completeness of the Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q. Dimon certifies that the report does not contain any misleading statements and that the financial statements fairly present the company's financial condition and results. The section outlines the responsibilities of the certifying officers in establishing disclosure controls and internal controls over financial reporting. It also details the evaluation of these controls and any changes that may have occurred during the reporting period, including disclosures of significant deficiencies or fraud related to internal controls.

children.title: Exhibit 31.2
children.summary: Exhibit 31.2 contains a certification by Jeremy Barnum, the Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of JPMorgan Chase & Co., regarding the accuracy and completeness of the Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q. It affirms that the report does not contain any misleading statements and that the financial statements fairly present the company's financial condition and results. The certification also outlines the responsibilities for establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting, including evaluations of their effectiveness and disclosures of any significant deficiencies or fraud. This section emphasizes the importance of transparency and accountability in financial reporting.

children.title: Exhibit 32
children.summary: Exhibit 32 contains a certification by JPMorgan Chase & Co. officers, including CEO James Dimon and CFO Jeremy Barnum, pursuant to 18 U.S.C. Section 1350 and Section 906 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002. The certification confirms that the Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the period ending June 30, 2023, complies with the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and accurately presents the company's financial condition and results of operations. This document is essential for ensuring accountability and transparency in financial reporting.
